Research programmes are developed together with companies, ranging from large multinational manufacturers to SMEs, ensuring that innovations address real industrial challenges and can be rapidly deployed in operational environments.

Through extensive collaborations with European partners, research organizations, and industrial clusters, it actively contributes to strengthening Europe's technological sovereignty, industrial competitiveness, and the transition towards sustainable manufacturing.

entityDescription: The association ROBOTIADA is a Lithuanian non-profit organization promoting interest in science, technology, engineering, robotics, and STEAM education among children, youth, teachers, and families. REOR20 AG is a Swiss deep-tech company developing advanced AI and geospatial technologies for real-time flood modelling and climate risk intelligence. Its core technology, DeepWater, is a physics-informed AI flood simulation platform that combines Earth observation, weather, terrain, land-cover and hydrological data to predict flood evolution and generate high-resolution flood hazard maps within minutes. The technology is designed to operate globally and across different flood mechanisms, including pluvial, fluvial and coastal flooding.
REOR20 develops solutions for flood risk assessment, climate resilience, disaster preparedness and response, infrastructure protection and insurance. The company integrates satellite and geospatial data with advanced numerical modelling and artificial intelligence to deliver rapid, scalable and location-independent flood intelligence for governments, infrastructure operators, insurers and other organisations exposed to flood risk.

The first EISCAT system was commissioned in 1981. Since then, our facilities have been continuously developed and expanded. Today it consist of world-leading incoherent scatter radar stations and an advanced ionospheric heating facility. All located in the northernmost part of the Nordic region in the Arctic.
EISCAT offers unique conditions for research in several fields. Our radar measurements make it possible to study phenomena such as the northern lights (aurora borealis), space weather and space debris, as well as atmospheric dynamics. Read more about the science here: The Science of EISCAT. All our radar stations are working together, providing researchers with unique opportunities for advanced studies in multiple dimensions.
EISCAT radars are used as both incoherent and coherent scatter radars to:
- study the properties and instabilities of the ionosphere.
- investigate the structure and dynamics of the atmosphere.
- conduct ionospheric modification experiments with the heating facility.
All data from our radar stations is only used for civil research.
Advanced research radar facilities in the Arctic
We are building a new next generation incoherent scatter research radar facility, to replace the old EISCAT system. EISCAT_3D is not yet operational.

Transition from EISCAT Scientific Association to EISCAT AB
EISCAT was founded in 1976 as a non-profit scientific association, formerly named EISCAT Scientific Association. The mission was to conduct research on the lower, middle and upper atmosphere and the ionosphere using incoherent scatter radar technique. This technology is the most powerful ground-based tool for such studies.
At the end of 2024, EISCAT transferred its assets to a Swedish limited company – EISCAT AB. The new company officially took over operations on 1 January 2025. The transition was motivated by both legal and security needs, particularly related to the development of the new EISCAT_3D radar system, and resulted in a more robust corporate structure.
The transition to a limited company was driven by changing legal requirements, as a result of EISCAT starting the construction of the EISCAT_3D infrastructure. The limited company form facilitates higher requirements for security, governance and finance compared to the previous association model. EISCAT AB is now a state-owned company with Sweden, Norway and Finland as owners. Other organisations, internationally, can apply to join as associates or affiliates. This structure provides a clearer division of responsibilities, more efficient decision-making and greater financial transparency – important factors for multinational scientific infrastructure.

Zenith Pulse GmbH — Company Description (EN)
Zenith Pulse GmbH is a German company based in Baden-Württemberg developing a software platform that calculates a company's actual carbon footprint directly from its suppliers' invoices, processed through a proprietary algorithm, and generates a Scope 1/2/3 emissions report with concrete reduction recommendations. Built on this core engine, Zenith Pulse is developing additional verticals that integrate Copernicus (Sentinel) and NASA Earth observation data to enrich the analysis with land-use monitoring, coastal-zone assessment, pollution and urban heat-island detection, physical climate risk, and resource-use intelligence.
The product addresses a regulatory-driven need: the EU Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) requires companies to report Scope 1/2/3 emissions, while smaller suppliers face indirect pressure to provide the same data to larger corporate customers. Target customers include both private companies (B2B) and German municipalities, served through modular subscription packages.
A working prototype of the core Scope 1/2/3 calculation engine is operational, using recognized, publicly documented emission-factor sources. The satellite-data verticals are in development and have not yet been validated with a paying customer.
The founding team combines engineering and entrepreneurial experience with software architecture and IoT research expertise, supported by a specialist in GIS and remote sensing for satellite data integration.

We develop highly perfected but easy to use metrology products and services. We are proud to work with companies of all sizes, from the smallest ones to the largest global corporations.
 
Work in the company is organized into two key areas, namely:
1. performing metrology solutions and,
2. research and development based on metrology field.
 
Metrology solutions:
In the LOTRIČ Metrology group, we perform calibrations for the widest range of customer requirements. The certificate is the key and most important result of the service execution. This certificate ensures the traceability of the customer's measuring instruments, providing tabular and graphical accuracy and precision results with measuring uncertainty. The calibration certificate complies with the necessary international standards (ISO 17020 and ISO 17025), technical guidelines, and customer-specific needs.
With 512 methods, of which 249 are accredited, we are the leading provider of all-in-one metrology solutions. We cover more than 95% of all metrological needs for most clients. Research and development:
In the scope of research and development, we focus on:
- advanced systems for measuring product dimensions that are fully tailored to the client’s needs.
- inline or Offline systems for complete quality control based on advanced algorithms
- advanced platforms for data processing that incorporate machine vision technology and predictive capabilities
- development of certification schemes for non-harmonized areas to verify device compliance before startup and during use (e.g., robotics), with monitoring of repeatability, accuracy, reliability, and other safety elements

description:
Henddu is a deep-tech environmental intelligence company that develops integrated systems for monitoring, modelling, and forecasting air quality and climate risk across Africa. Combining satellite data, IoT sensor networks, and AI analytics, Henddu provides governments, industries, and research institutions with real-time insights into pollutant dynamics and related risks.

Our multidisciplinary team—comprising engineers, atmospheric scientists, and data specialists—addresses a critical systemic gap in environmental intelligence across Africa and other developing regions: the near-total absence of reliable, localized, and actionable air-quality and climate-risk data, despite the continent bearing some of the world’s highest pollution burdens.

Henddu is committed to transforming environmental data into actionable intelligence. From urban micro-stations to regional modelling, we bridge the information gap that has long constrained effective environmental management and public-health protection in Africa.
entityDescription:
Henddu is a France-based startup that develops smart air quality and climate observatories tailored for developing countries starting in Africa. By leveraging a digital platform powered by proprietary algorithms, Henddu offers a cost-effective solution—up to 6 times cheaper in capital expenditure and 10 times in operating costs than traditional systems. The platform integrates diverse data sources including satellite Earth observation, ground sensors, meteorology, and health indicators to provide real-time environmental intelligence. Its space-based data fusion, using services like Sentinel and CAMS, enables hyperlocal pollution forecasting (HOQA), hotspot detection (Henddu-Spot), and vulnerability mapping (Henddu-Cluster). This multidimensional approach strengthens public policy, institutional capacity, and community engagement through actionable, data-driven insights. Henddu empowers governments and industries to shift from passive monitoring to predictive and strategic environmental governance—driven by both space and ground intelligence.
Henddu is supported by Inria Startup Studio, ESA BIC Nord France, Euratechnologies and the French Public Investment Bank (Bpifrance), and collaborates closely with academic partners such as Inria, the University of Lille, and CNES.
